themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints exploded to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting either a recent disease outbreak, storm damage, or pest infestation affecting the Upper East Side's street canopy.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average per week over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase)
Z-score of 11.72 indicates statistically extreme deviation—among highest in dataset
No corresponding Reddit or local news coverage yet, suggesting emerging story with first-mover advantage
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks to determine if this reflects a new disease, pest (emerald ash borer, etc.), or weather event
Canvass affected blocks to document visible tree condition and gather resident concerns about canopy loss
Check if spike correlates with recent weather or infrastructure work that may have stressed trees

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints surged to 52 last week versus a baseline of 23.8 per week—a 119% spike (z-score: 5.34)—alongside a spike in dumpster complaints (4 this week vs. 0.4 average, +967%) and litter basket requests (6 last week vs. 1.2 average, +380%), indicating a deteriorating sanitation environment across the district.
evidence: Unsanitary condition complaints: 52 last week vs. 23.8 weekly average (119% increase, z-score 5.34)
Dumpster complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.4 average (967% increase, z-score 7.49)
Litter basket requests: 6 last week vs. 1.2 average (380% increase, z-score 7.18)
Triple convergence of related sanitation spikes suggests systematic failure, not isolated complaints
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY to determine if staffing, routes, or collection schedules have changed; check for labor actions or budget cuts
Map complaint locations to identify whether spike is concentrated (single neighborhood) or distributed (district-wide)
Canvass residents and business owners for firsthand observations of trash accumulation and rodent/pest activity

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs spiked to 9 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 1.4 average (554% increase, z-score 6.86), paired with missing street signs (7 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.2 average, +460%, z-score 5.94), indicating accelerating physical decay of street-level infrastructure across the district.
evidence: Damaged street signs: 9 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average (554% increase, z-score 6.86)
Missing street signs: 7 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (460% increase, z-score 5.94)
Two related infrastructure issues spiking simultaneously suggests deferred maintenance or budget constraint
Street condition already ranks 3rd in overall 311 complaint volume (1,078 total over 90 days)
reporting_angles: File FOIL to DOT to obtain complaint data and departmental response times for UES street sign repairs
Walk major intersections to verify scope and safety impact of missing/damaged signage
Interview DOT about prioritization—whether UES is being deprioritized relative to other districts

themes_detail.label: Animal Incidents in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints surged to 9 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.2 per week—a 300% spike (z-score: 6.19)—suggesting either a pest/wildlife encroachment issue or increased public awareness, with implications for park safety and public health.
evidence: Animal-in-park complaints: 9 two weeks ago vs. 2.2 weekly average (300% increase, z-score 6.19)
No recent local news coverage of animal issues in UES parks, suggesting emerging story
Timing overlaps with potential urban wildlife season shift (spring/early summer activity increase)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and NYC Health to determine what animals are being reported and whether intervention is underway
Canvass parks (Central Park, Carl Schurz Park, etc.) to document visible wildlife presence and user concerns
Interview Parks maintenance staff on whether there has been a policy or staffing change affecting wildlife management

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis (Persistent)
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints remain the 2nd-highest category in the district with 1,126 complaints over 90 days, reflecting an ongoing structural issue in housing stock; while not a new spike, this chronic problem aligns with repeated community board budget requests for NYCHA facility renovation.
evidence: 1,126 heat/hot water complaints over 90-day period (2nd-highest category after illegal parking)
Community board has requested NYCHA facility renovation funding for multiple consecutive budget cycles, indicating unresolved systemic problem
High volume suggests issue affects renters across multiple buildings, not isolated failures
reporting_angles: Analyze 311 heat complaint data by address to identify buildings with chronic violations; cross-reference with HPD violations and NYCHA status
Interview tenants in affected buildings to document health impacts, habitability concerns, and enforcement frustration
Investigate whether landlords are systematically deprioritizing heat system maintenance and what enforcement tools HPD is using
